findings.title: Splash and portrait cards are posterized model renders composited onto plates, all in one framing
findings.what: Every card is a filtered game render pasted into the right third of the frame. Light does not match: in splash.png a flat pale figure stands against an orange-lit dusk city. The base splash face reads as carved blocks.
findings.evidence: Viewed art/out/fighters/nurrow/splash.png and nurrow_noon_fair_splash.png. _harness/_reports/closing_nurrow_cardqa.txt: mass x 0.702 / 0.724 / 0.709, feet 0.924 / 0.931 / 0.920; fig grain p50 4.8-6.5 vs plate 0.4-1.0.
findings.gauge: LoL ships a per-skin painted splash with its own composition and light unified with the scene.
findings.fix: Paint over the render, relight it to the plate, and vary camera and placement per skin, staged in Nurrow's world (lamp alley, fair lanterns, woodblock shadows).
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced the placement numbers and checked the images myself. card_qa gates pass, so this is an art-quality major, not a gate failure.

findings.title: Noon Fair portrait and splash: the face is an unreadable smeared mass under a clawing hand
findings.what: The hand covers the mask; after posterizing, the mask is warped tan streaks. It is not a sensitivity blocker: the in-game mask is clean, and the streaks read as melted, not horror.
findings.evidence: _harness/_shots/closing_nurrow_face_nurrow_noon_fair_portrait_x3.png, viewed; nurrow_noon_fair_splash.png at ~1150-1300 x 180-300 shows the same smear.
findings.gauge: A LoL store splash keeps a clean, deliberate face read as the focal point.
findings.fix: Re-pose to a hush finger at the mask lips, mask the face out of the median pass, and hand-paint the lids.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed visually. It stays major, not a blocker, because the face is distorted but not a horror read.

findings.title: Lunges and the ult read as a cream disc on legs; the blade points down and the cape snaps 102 deg in one frame
findings.what: In cast_a1 frames 4-8 and the ult lunge, the hat disc covers the torso and the blade trails at the floor. At the ult, the cape flips up as a sheet in one frame.
findings.evidence: _harness/_shots/closing_nurrow_cliprow_a1.png and closing_nurrow_cliprow_ult.png, viewed; closing_nurrow_three_gamecam_row2.png shows a disc over the body top-down; _harness/_reports/closing_nurrow_chain.txt cast_ult max step 70.1 / 102.2 deg (other clips at most 14.8).
findings.gauge: A LoL assassin's dash and ult keep a readable action line with the weapon leading and no one-frame cloth pops.
findings.fix: Counter-pitch the head and hat 15-20 deg in the lunges, lead with the blade level at impact, and re-bake the ult cape with substeps or a ~30 deg per-frame clamp.
findings.verifierNote: Confirmed. Mitigation: at side angles in the match (closing_nurrow_ingame_casts_x2.png, panels 1-2) the lunge diagonal does read, so it is not worse than major.
